title: Tether landing page: choose the structure
question: The visual world is fixed (Tether's Liquid Glass over the pixel landscape). These are three ways to build the page. Lock one, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: Press ⌘K
options.thesis: The page is driven like the app: a glass command palette over the landscape is the hero and the navigation.
options.viewport: A large open palette centred over the day/night scenery; first row 'Download for macOS' is highlighted and Enter downloads. Rows for Windows, Linux and each tour filter as you type.
options.risk: A visitor who never types sees a list before they see the product window.

options.label: Request ↔ Response
options.thesis: Every section is a request on the left and Tether's real answer on the right, joined by a {{@reference}}.
options.viewport: Left: URL capsule 'GET tether.app/download' with Send. Right: the response pane, 200 OK, whose JSON lists the installers as working download links.
options.risk: The pairing repeats each section and could feel mechanical; it stacks on phones.

options.label: Send it
options.thesis: The hero is one giant URL capsule; pressing Send runs a real request and the full Tether window unfolds with the answer.
options.viewport: Huge glass URL bar with method and accent Send, the plane gliding above; on Send the pulse plays, status/time/size land and a window replica grows below with download buttons in its response.
options.risk: Leans on a live third-party API; needs a canned fallback when offline.
